subject: Embeddings sidecar egress & archival policy for partner stores
messages:
From: Lee Wong <partners@orion-storage.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Embeddings sidecar egress & archival policy for partner stores

Hi Rafael / Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick chat at last week's partner forum. We came away with a few specific asks from our engineering team around how Redwood would handle embeddings egress and long-term archival when an embeddings sidecar is colocated with a customer's S3-backed vector store (pgvector + S3 for large objects). The areas they'd like clarity on: 

- Where do tokenized embeddings leave Redwood network (egress points) when we run the sidecar in the customer VPC?
- Retention / TTL semantics for KV cache vs. persistent index objects and how Redwood signals deletions to downstream stores
- A recommended minimal SLA for restore/archive requests when we trigger a cold-restore from S3 (we operate on tight RTOs)

We have a security/compliance questionnaire coming Friday and they'd prefer we attach a short policy summary describing the flow and controls. Can you share a short policy statement or draft (PDF or Google Doc) and a simple CSV matrix with expected latencies for cold restores across typical object sizes?

Happy to set a 30min technical sync this week if that helps.

Thanks,
Lee
—
Lee Wong
Director, Integrations — Orion Storage
partners@orion-storage.com

Attachments: none

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 12:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings sidecar egress & archival policy for partner stores

Team — forwarding Lee's note from Orion. Short summary of their asks above.

Quick thoughts:
- Egress: for Private (VPC) sidecar deployments we don't route payloads through hosted gateways; the sidecar emits only model call telemetry (anonymized) back to Redwood control plane. Embedding vectors destined for S3/pgvector can be written directly from the sidecar to the customer's S3 endpoint or to the customer's DB endpoint over the VPC. That means egress points are customer-controlled; we should state that clearly.
- Retention: we currently maintain a soft KV cache (ephemeral, default 24h) and separately a persistence write stream. Deletion/TTL should be an explicit API event the sidecar sends (we have a delete webhook option) — confirm with infra if webhook is durable across outages.
- Cold restore SLA: we have existing tests for object sizes up to 2GB, median restore ~90s in us-west with our S3 helper; for larger objects we fall back to streaming reads.

Action: Vanessa / Kimberly can you draft a 1‑page policy summary + a CSV with two latency columns (small object <10MB, large object 100–200MB) and include a short note on proof-of-delete mechanics? If we have a one-pager by Wed EOD we can attach it to their questionnaire. I'll offer a sync slot.

R

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Embeddings sidecar egress & archival policy for partner stores

Lee — thanks for the clear ask. Rafael pushed this over; I attached a short draft (egress_policy_draft.pdf) and a latency matrix (embeddings-ttl-matrix.csv). Highlights in the doc: 

- Control plane vs data plane separation: we explicitly state that embeddings written by the sidecar go directly to customer-managed endpoints. Redwood control plane receives only metadata and optional telemetry.
- Egress points: we enumerate the two supported egress modes (direct S3 write, direct DB insert) and call out network-level requirements (VPC endpoint / NAT) and recommended CIDR allow-lists for initial provisioning.
- Retention model: default KV cache TTL is 24 hours; persistence writes are customer-owned. Delete/retention requests are implemented via idempotent delete APIs; sidecar will return a proof-of-delete token that can be verified against the customer's object metadata.
- Cold-restore SLA guidance: suggested target RTOs: 2–3 min for <50MB objects, 5–8 min for 50–500MB under typical us-west conditions. We include fallback patterns (range reads, parallel chunking).

Link to editable draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-orion-egress-draft
Doc attached as PDF per your questionnaire requirement.

Next steps:
1) If this looks good, I'd propose a 30-min tech review Thurs 9/3 10am PT — Rafael, Ben, Kimberly, will you join?
2) We can add a short FAQ section for the security questionnaire with proof-of-delete implementation details.

Thanks — Vanessa

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Alliances, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

Attachments: egress_policy_draft.pdf, embeddings-ttl-matrix.csv

- For large object restores we prefer a worst-case SLA line item we can present to procurement (they asked for a single number). Would Redwood be comfortable committing to a 10-minute SLA for restores of objects up to 500MB when sidecar is deployed in us-west?

Happy to take the Thurs 9/3 10am PT slot if you confirm. We'll forward the questionnaire once you add the two bullets above.

Thanks,
Lee
